newsitem.title: ECUADOR: PETROECUADOR RAISES CRUDE OIL PRICE BY 40 CENTS.
newsitem.headline: PETROECUADOR RAISES CRUDE OIL PRICE BY 40 CENTS.

text.p: Ecuador's state-owned oil company Petroecuador has raised its sale price of crude oil by 40 cents in order to raise more revenue, the company said Friday.
"Petroecuador decided to raise by 40 cents the sale price for destinations that use the West Texas Intermediate (WTI) measure of prices," Petroecuador said in a statement.
It added that the increase comes after two adjustments in the WTI formula between June and August.
The first rise of 30 cents, which took place between June and July, led to an increase in daily income of $3.46 million to the state.
The second rise of 10 cents since the beginning of August, raised the daily income $86,000 further.
"The increases in crude prices have been achieved despite the announced return to the international markets by Iraq, once the United Nations agreements have been concluded," the statement said.
Ecuador adopted the WTI price formula in May, after using the West Texas Sour (WTS) measure since October last year.
Ecuadorean crude cost an average $14.62 per barrel in July, lower than the $15 anticipated in the government's 1997 budget.
